statement: A librarian asked $24$ students how many library books each of them borrowed last month. The results are shown in the table. $$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Books borrowed} & \text{Number of students} \\ \hline 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 7 \\ 2 & 6 \\ 3 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 \end{array}$$ What is the median number of books borrowed by these students?

choices.misconception: I computed the mean number of books, $39 \div 24$, instead of the median.
I took the middle value of the list 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 in the first column without counting how many students gave each answer.
I found the median of the second column, the numbers of students, which is 5.

hints: With $24$ values, the median is the average of two middle values. Which positions are they?
List the values in order using the counts: the first $5$ values are $0$, the next $7$ are $1$, and so on. Find the $12$th and $13$th values.
The values $0$ fill positions $1$ to $5$ and the values $1$ fill positions $6$ to $12$, so the $12$th value is $1$ and the $13$th value is $2$.

solutions.reliable: There are $24$ students, so the median is the mean of the $12$th and $13$th values in order. The running totals are $5$ (through $0$ books), $12$ (through $1$ book) and $18$ (through $2$ books). The $12$th value is $1$ and the $13$th value is $2$, so the median is $\dfrac{1 + 2}{2} = 1.5$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
